canonical_name: LMDB 0.9.31 -- Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (Howard Chu, Symas / OpenLDAP)
lineage: B+tree key-value store with single-writer/multi-reader MVCC and copy-on-write pages: crash consistency WITHOUT a write-ahead log (two meta pages, the last committed root wins). Descends from OpenLDAP's back-mdb work (2011); rival to Berkeley DB and to log-structured stores such as LevelDB.
entry_points: mdb_env_open / mdb_txn_begin / mdb_put / mdb_txn_commit; mtest.c .. mtest6.c drivers; mdb_stat, mdb_dump

example.output: verified cursor scans; a testdb/ file

upstream_docs: Chu, The Lightning Memory-Mapped Database (LMDB), 2012-; libraries/liblmdb/lmdb.h

human_capability_summary.built_to: give readers a consistent snapshot while one writer commits, and survive a crash at any instant without replaying a log
human_capability_summary.pressure: concurrent readers and a writer on one file; power loss mid-write; bounded memory via the OS page cache
human_capability_summary.success_means: every reader sees a committed root; after a crash the database opens at the last committed state with no repair step

known_human_problem_solved: crash-consistent concurrent key-value storage without a log
human_environmental_pressure: competing writers/readers, partial failure (crash mid-commit), bounded memory
human_failure_condition: a torn write corrupts the tree, or a reader observes a half-committed page
behavioral_entry_point: kill the process between mdb_put and mdb_txn_commit (or run mtest with a small map size) and reopen: the previous root is what comes back

lineage_relations.note: rival designs for the same problem: copy-on-write B+tree vs log-structured merge

nyx_handoff.how_to_run_it: recipe.json (runner docker); python -m techne.fossils.harvest run lmdb-0.9.31
nyx_handoff.what_humans_used_it_for: give readers a consistent snapshot while one writer commits, and survive a crash at any instant without replaying a log
